chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from a number of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The right of the traveller is that his companions stay with him (stand over him) when he is sick, for three (days).'
ai.seo_question: What is the duration and nature of care companions must provide to a sick traveller according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith establishes the specific duration of three days for companions to attend to a sick traveler, reflecting the practical social ethics of early Islamic communities. It underscores the concept of *haqq* (right) in companionship, emphasizing communal responsibility and care during vulnerability, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding social duties.
